column3: The Hebrew pictures protection as setting him on high.
The Hebrew has a singular burnt offering and a verb of making fat; BSB uses plural offerings and look favorably.
The Hebrew says according to your heart without explicitly supplying desires.
The Hebrew presents saving His anointed as completed; BSB uses saves.
The Hebrew says we mention or remember the name, not explicitly trust, and leaves the first clauses verbless.
The Hebrew presents these actions as completed; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew has a third-person verb for answering, with the king as subject; BSB directly commands Answer us.
